piece_type: Consumer website webpages ('What is Recorlev?' and 'Taking Recorlev')

cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “The SONICS clinical study supported the efficacy and safety results from LOGICS” o “31% of patients had normal cortisol levels after taking Recorlev for 6 months without changing their dose” o “67% of patients who moved on to the second part of the study had normal cortisol levels by the end of the study”
cases.context: PI: 29/77 (38%) normal at end of maintenance; 16/77 (21%) at end of extended evaluation; 67% was end of titration; PI caveat that 51% discontinued prematurely omitted.
cases.rationale: 67% misstates the timepoint and overstates efficacy; omits material discontinuation caveat.
cases.check: Rule: verify each quoted percentage matches the label value for the stated timepoint/phase; flag omission of label 'interpret with caution' caveats.

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (enriched/randomized-withdrawal subset)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Claims about Efficacy
cases.claim: “Recorlev - More patients (52%) who were on a stable and steady dose of Recorlev had normal cortisol levels”
cases.context: 52% = 11/21 randomized-withdrawal patients selected from 79 who had tolerated and responded.
cases.rationale: Enriched responder subset presented as general patient experience.
cases.check: Are results from an enriched/randomized-withdrawal population presented as representative of all patients?

cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: “As with other medicines for Cushing's, monitoring by your doctor is important so they know how you're doing” . . . “Heart and liver tests before and during treatment with Recorlev will help your doctor avoid side effects” | “Side effects can occur with Recorlev, including some that are serious”
cases.context: Boxed warnings for hepatotoxicity and QT prolongation (13% DILI; 14.7% QTcF change >60 msec); boxed warnings relegated to middle of ISI without signal.
cases.rationale: Generic risk statement omits boxed warnings and implies monitoring lets patients 'avoid' side effects.
cases.check: Rule: flag generic risk statements ('side effects can occur', 'some serious') and 'avoid side effects' language when the product has a boxed warning; boxed warning must lead the ISI.
